newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to discuss new U.S. force for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to discuss new U.S. force for Bosnia.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will discuss an extension of U.S. troop involvement in Bosnia at a news conference on Friday, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

McCurry told reporters Clinton would "advise the American people the thinking of the United States as we prepare for deliberations in NATO on the question of the future of Bosnia and how we can maintain a secure and safe environment as the peace process continues."

McCurry said a plan for a follow-up force in Bosnia might be crafted by the North Atlantic Council by early December, but offered no details on how many U.S. troops might be involved, or how large the total force would be.

He said Defence Secretary William Perry and Gen. John Shalikashvili, chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, would be briefing at 1:30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT) and might have more details on the maximum size of any extension force.

Representatives to the North Atlantic Council, NATO's political arm, will meet with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana in Brussels on Monday and are expected to recommend formal approval of a new peacekeeping force by Western governments, NATO officials said.
In Washington this week Solana said he had been given to understand the United States would take part in a future force and said he expected 7,000 to 8,000 U.S. troops to be involved.
